# Real spatial transcriptomics workflow

This chapter uses two real SCOP datasets: 1,986 human PanIN Visium spots from GSM8058244 and 2,000 spots across two mouse-brain slices.

## 1 · Load and audit coordinate space

```r
library(scop)
library(Seurat)

data(visium_human_pancreas_sub, package = "scop")
srt <- visium_human_pancreas_sub
DefaultAssay(srt) <- "Spatial"

dim(srt)
Images(srt)
head(srt[[]][, c("x", "y", "sample_id", "coda_label")])
```

Confirm whether coordinates are raw array coordinates, image pixels, or a display transform. The published workflow uses `coord.cols = c("x", "y")` consistently.

## 2 · Spot QC

```r
srt <- RunSpotQC(
  srt,
  assay = "Spatial",
  return_filtered = FALSE,
  qc_metrics = c("umi", "gene", "mito"),
  UMI_threshold = 0,
  gene_threshold = 0,
  mito_threshold = 100
)
```

Those permissive values compute and retain metrics for the bundled teaching subset; they are not recommended thresholds for raw tissue. For a new slide, inspect spot distributions, tissue mask, empty/background spots, spatial edge effects, and per-slice retention before filtering.

## 3 · Normalise and find spatially variable genes

```r
srt <- NormalizeData(srt, assay = "Spatial")
srt <- RunSpatialVariableFeatures(
  srt,
  assay = "Spatial",
  method = "moran",
  coord.cols = c("x", "y"),
  nfeatures = 100,
  min_spots = 10,
  seed = 20260807
)
head(VariableFeatures(srt), 20)
```

The top real Moran features include `FBP1`, `CELA3A`, `PNLIP`, `SPP1`, `CLPS`, `CTRC`, `PRSS1`, and `COL1A1`.

![Human PanIN spatial domains and the top Moran feature FBP1.](assets/figures/real-data/spatial-human-pancreas.png){fig-alt="Two tissue-coordinate panels show CoDa domain labels and FBP1 log expression across 1,986 real Visium spots."}

Most spots are labelled collagen in this subset, while islet, acinar, smooth-muscle, fat, epithelial, and rare PanIN-labelled spots occupy smaller regions. The plot is spot-level evidence.

## 4 · Build the spatial graph and neighbourhood summary

```r
srt <- RunSpatialNetwork(
  srt,
  method = "knn",
  image = "slice1",
  coord.cols = c("x", "y"),
  k = 6,
  graph.name = "scop_knn"
)

srt <- RunSpatialNeighborhood(
  srt,
  group.by = "coda_label",
  method = "observed",
  image = "slice1",
  coord.cols = c("x", "y"),
  k = 6,
  tool_name = "coda_neighborhood"
)
```

Application: describe which labelled spot domains lie next to one another. With multiple patients, carry `sample.by`/`subject.by` through and model associations across independent tissues.

## 5 · Deconvolution choices

If a matched single-cell reference exists, SCOP exposes `RunRCTD()`:

```r
rctd <- RunRCTD(
  srt = srt,
  reference = reference,
  reference_label = "cell_type",
  coord.cols = c("x", "y"),
  rctd_mode = "full"
)
```

The audited runtime lacks `spacexr`, so no RCTD result is shown. Deconvolution requires compatible species, gene identifiers, reference cell types, and a functioning backend. A domain label is not a substitute for cell-composition estimation.

## 6 · Multiple slides

```r
data(visium_mouse_brain_slices_sub, package = "scop")
table(visium_mouse_brain_slices_sub$slice)
Images(visium_mouse_brain_slices_sub)
```

![Two real mouse-brain Visium slices before integration.](assets/figures/real-data/spatial-mouse-brain-slices.png){fig-alt="Two panels show 1,000 sampled spots from each of two sagittal anterior mouse-brain Visium slices."}

Do QC and spatial-feature discovery per slide, preserve `sample_id` and coordinate systems, and only then consider `RunSpatialIntegration()`. Integration across slides must not erase a biological region or condition that is confounded with slide.

::: {.boundary}
Visium spots are mixtures. Moran features and neighbourhoods support spatial-pattern claims; they do not prove cell-resolved identity, interaction, or causality.
:::
